intro.TrustedMarkup:
The .vyx single-file component compiler, in comptime-pure Vyrn.

components(dir) reads every <Name>.vyx in dir at compile time and synthesizes one module that exports one pure view function per component, built from std/html calls. std/ui's pages reuses the compiler core (vyxCompileComponent, vyxBuildModule) for .vyx pages.

import { components } from "std/vyx"
import { itemRow, cart } from components("./components")

A .vyx file has two sections:

<script>   -- optional: a `props { name: Type, ... }` block (the view fn's
             parameters), `import` lines (relative paths rebased to the
             synthesized module, deduplicated across components), and
             plain `fn`/`let`/`type` helpers (module-private).
<template> -- exactly one root element, compiled to the view fn body.

Template grammar (Vue-flavored):

{{ expr }}                  -> text((expr).toString())     (escaped)
v-html="expr"               -> Raw(expr) as the element's content; `expr` is a
                              `Markup`, which `Raw` never escapes
<slot/>                     -> splices the trailing children param
v-if="c" / v-else-if="c" / v-else   -> nested Empty-elided conditionals; a
                              v-else-if/v-else must be the next element
                              sibling (whitespace and comments between are
                              fine)
v-for="x in expr"  (+ required :key="expr")   -> keyed loop
:name="expr"  (incl. :class, :value)          -> dynamic attribute
name="..."                  -> static attribute (`class` is checked when
                              themed)
<Capitalized :p="e" q="s"/> / <Capitalized>...</Capitalized>  -> component call
@click="handler" / @click="handler(scalar)" (also @input/@change/@submit/...)
                            -> On(event, "handler", (scalar).toString())

Whitespace: an all-whitespace run that spans a newline is dropped; a same-line whitespace run is one space; other runs collapse to single spaces. <!-- ... --> comments are inert, and a lone { in text is literal.

Every generation failure is a std/diag report at the .vyx line it came from. vyrn emit-gen <file> shows the synthesized module.

Generation-time components. A capitalized tag resolves first against sibling .vyx files, then against names the <script> sections import. An imported name is a provider: std/vyx emits a nested generator import that runs the imported gen fn with the tag's attributes as constant arguments, and splices its output where the tag stood.

<script>
import { Icon } from "./icon-provider"
</script>
<template>
<p><Icon name="brand:github" label="GitHub"/></p>
</template>

A provider is an ordinary module that exports a gen fn of this shape:

export gen fn <TagName>(attrs: String, file: String, line: Int64, col: Int64) -> String

attrs  the tag's static attributes as a JSON object of strings, in source
       order, written by `std/json` so `std/jsonread` reads it back exactly;
       `{}` when there are none.
file   the `.vyx` file the tag was written in.
line   the tag's 1-based line in that file.
col    always 1: a template node carries no column.

The generated module must export

export fn provide() -> Html

which std/vyx calls at the tag site through a namespace alias it mints. The name is not render: a user function named after a surface builtin shadows it program-wide, so it would break render here.

A provider tag takes static attributes only and no children; :attr, @event and children are diagnostics. Compute a value in a sibling .vyx component instead. The provider runs in its own sandbox and cache entry, and anchors its own reports at the file/line it is given. std/vyx cannot check the provider's shape, because a template-named provider is outside its read roots; a wrong shape fails the emitted import with the loader's diagnostic.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type VyxAttr = { name: String, value: String, dyn: Bool, evt: Bool, line: Int64, col: Int64 }

prose.TrustedMarkup: One attribute on a template element. dyn: a :name="expr" value; evt: an @event binding, @ stripped. A v-... directive is a plain attribute that keeps its v- prefix and is consumed by the grouping pass. line/col: the 1-based position of the value in the .vyx file.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type VyxNode = enum { VNText(String), VNInterp(String, Int64, Int64), VNRaw(String, Int64, Int64), VNChildren, VNElem(String, Bool, Array<VyxAttr>, Array<VyxNode>, Int64), VNIf(Array<String>, Array<Int64>, Array<Int64>, Array<VyxBody>, VyxBody, Bool), VNFor(String, String, String, Array<VyxNode>, Int64, Int64, Int64, Int64) }

prose.TrustedMarkup: A node in a parsed template. Lines are absolute in the .vyx file. A trailing (line, col) pair is the pass-through's position for origin directives; VNFor carries its iterable's, then its key's, and VNIf carries parallel per-condition position arrays.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type VyxBody = { nodes: Array<VyxNode> }

prose.TrustedMarkup: A node list, so bodies can nest in a payload without Array<Array<...>>.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type VyxTemplate = { nodes: Array<VyxNode>, err: String }

prose.TrustedMarkup: The parsed <template> of a .vyx source: its sibling nodes, or the err that stopped the parse.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxParseTemplate(source: String) -> VyxTemplate

prose.TrustedMarkup: Parses only the <template> section of a .vyx source into the node tree the compiler walks, for checking libraries such as std/vyx-hints. No props, imports, component resolution or v-if grouping: directives stay attributes. err is non-empty when the template does not parse.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxCompileComponent(compName: String, source: String, dir: String) -> VyxComp

prose.TrustedMarkup: Compiles one .vyx source into a VyxComp; component calls are resolved later, once every sibling name is known. compName is the file stem; dir rebases relative imports. Exported for std/ui's pages.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxBuildModule(comps: consume Array<VyxComp>, themed: Bool, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Assembles the synthesized module. When themed, it imports the theme theme (resolved like dir) and routes every class through vyxTheme.cls(...). Exported for std/ui's pages.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn components(dir: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Compiles every <Name>.vyx under dir into one module exporting one view per component. class is unchecked; componentsThemed checks it.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn componentsThemed(dir: String, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: components with a theme: the module imports tw(<theme>) as vyxTheme, a static class literal is checked against Tw at compile time at its .vyx position, and a dynamic :class is coerced at run time. theme resolves relative to the importing module, like dir.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn vyxDataForm(ret: String) -> Int64

prose.TrustedMarkup:
Which alternative signature of the std/ui:Page data member a return-type spelling names, numbered as matchedMember reports, or -1 for none:

0  `Query<T>`            blocking, no params
1  `Lazy<T>`             render-then-fill, no params
2  `ParamQuery<P, T>`    blocking, deferred call takes `Params`
3  `ParamLazy<P, T>`     render-then-fill, deferred call takes `Params`

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn vyxDataFormIsLazy(form: Int64) -> Bool

prose.TrustedMarkup: Whether a data form renders lazily.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn vyxDataFormHasParams(form: Int64) -> Bool

prose.TrustedMarkup: Whether a data form's deferred call takes the page's Params.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn vyxDataRunner(form: Int64) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: The std/ui runner that turns a data form into the loaded value.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn vyxQueryDataType(ret: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: The data type a data return-type spelling carries ("" when ret is none of the four): the last type argument, since a params type comes first. This is what the synthesized load() returns. Exported so std/ui reads a .vyrn page's data the same way.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxPageInterface(source: String) -> ModuleInterface

prose.TrustedMarkup: The public surface of a .vyx page's <script>, its statement-leading export fn declarations, as reflection for a contract check. The page has no moduleInterface, so this reads the source; unexported helpers are outside the contract.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxPageShape(source: String) -> VyxPageShape

prose.TrustedMarkup: Reflects a .vyx page's <script>: its params fields and loader. err is set on a malformed params block. Exported for std/ui.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxBuildPageModule(source: String, dir: String, themed: Bool, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Builds a .vyx page module: the template compiles to a uiPageBody(<params>[, data: Data]) view, and the module exports page and Params. Origins point at a synthetic UiPageBody.vyx; the unit tests use it.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxBuildPageClientModuleAt(source: String, srcPath: String, dir: String, themed: Bool, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: vyxBuildPageModuleAt for the client bundle: load and its dead imports are stripped and head/headTitle omitted. The view, Params and page are the server module's, byte for byte.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxBuildPageModuleAt(source: String, srcPath: String, dir: String, themed: Bool, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: vyxBuildPageModule with the real route-file path: when srcPath is set, origins target the real .vyx. The generated code is the same either way.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxPage(vyxPath: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Synthesizes a .vyx page module from vyxPath. The argument is the full .vyx path, because the generator sandbox admits reads of exactly its path arguments.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxPageThemed(vyxPath: String, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: vyxPage with the page's classes checked against theme.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxPageClient(vyxPath: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: vyxPage for the client bundle: no load, head or title, for std/ui's pagesClient.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxPageClientThemed(vyxPath: String, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: vyxPageClient with classes checked against theme.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxBuildLayoutModule(source: String, dir: String, themed: Bool, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Builds a .vyx layout module: layout(children: Array<Html>) -> Html around the compiled template, which must contain <slot/>, plus head() and headTitle().

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxBuildLayoutModuleAt(source: String, srcPath: String, dir: String, themed: Bool, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: vyxBuildLayoutModule with the real layout.vyx path for origins.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxLayout(vyxPath: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Synthesizes a .vyx layout module from vyxPath.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxLayoutThemed(vyxPath: String, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: vyxLayout with the layout's classes checked against theme.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxBuildErrorModule(source: String, dir: String, themed: Bool, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Builds a .vyx error module: errorPage(e: PageError) -> Html around the compiled template, with the injected error prop.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxBuildErrorModuleAt(source: String, srcPath: String, dir: String, themed: Bool, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: vyxBuildErrorModule with the real error.vyx path. The injected PageError import has no origin.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxError(vyxPath: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Synthesizes a .vyx error-page module from vyxPath.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn vyxErrorThemed(vyxPath: String, theme: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: vyxError with classes checked against theme.
